name: Battle of Varna, Last Crusade Against the Turks
summary: The last major Western crusading effort against the Ottomans ends in disaster at Varna. King Vladislaus III of Poland-Hungary breaks a recently signed peace treaty with the Ottomans at papal urging; the resulting battle kills the king and destroys the Polish-Hungarian army. Sultan Murad II's victory ensures Ottoman control of the Balkans and removes the last serious external military threat to Constantinople before the final siege (1453).

_quarry.structural_significance: Varna removes Hungary's best army and most capable royal line; John Hunyadi survives and continues resistance but cannot prevent Constantinople's fall nine years later; the battle's outcome demonstrates that papal exhortations to crusade could override prudent military calculation with catastrophic results; the defeat makes the fall of Constantinople in 1453 effectively inevitable by eliminating the only force that could have relieved the city
